source_text: εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν, διὰ παντὸς εἰσίασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες. Εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν, ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος, ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων, τοῦτο δηλοῦντος τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, μήπω πεφανερῶσθαι τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὁδὸν, ἔτι τῆς πρώτης σκηνῆς ἐχούσης στάσιν. Ἥτις παραβολὴ εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τὸν ἐνεστηκότα, καθ' ὃν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίαι προσφέρονται, μὴ δυνάμεναι κατὰ συνείδησιν τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα, μόνον ἐπὶ βρώμασι καὶ πόμασι καὶ διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς δικαιώματα σαρκὸς μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως ἐπικείμενα. Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς οὐ χειροποιήτου, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως, οὐδὲ δι' αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος.» Συνίης οὖν ὅτι τὰς μὲν ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ λατρείας ἐπετέλουν οἱ ἱερεῖς, τὴν εἰς Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων εἰσδρομὴν οὐκ ἔχοντες. Τοιάδε γάρ πώς ἐστιν ἡ κατὰ νόμον λατρεία, στάσιν ἔχουσα τὴν ἐν σκιαῖς. Εἰκαῖα δὲ ταῦτα πρὸς κάθαρσιν καὶ ἀπόπλυσιν ἁμαρτίας. Διεπύθου γὰρ ἀρτίως βοῶντος τοῦ Παύλου, ὡς ἀνικάνως ἔχουσι κατὰ συνείδησιν, τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα. Διετηρεῖτο δὲ μᾶλλον μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως τοῦ Μονογενοῦς, ὅτε τῶν τύπων τὸ ἀκαλλὲς μετακεχώρηκεν εἰς ἀλήθειαν. «Ἅπαξ δὲ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ καὶ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων εἰσέθει. Καὶ οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος, ὃ προσῆγεν ὑπέρ τε ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων.» Σαφηνιεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τοῦτο πάλιν ὁ σοφώτατος Παῦλος ὡδὶ λέγων περὶ Χριστοῦ, «Ἀνώτερον λέγων, ὅτι θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας, οὔτε ηὐδόκησας, αἵτινες κατὰ νόμον προσφέρονται. Τότε εἶπον, Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου·» ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ· «Ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ἐσμὲν, διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἀρχιερεὺς ἕστηκε καθ' ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν, καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας, οὐδεμίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν, εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ· τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ, μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους.» Ἅπαξ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν, οὐκέτι ἀποθνήσκει, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον· πολλῶν δὲ ἀνενεγκὼν ἁμαρτίας, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, νῦν ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ προσώπῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Σαφὴς ὁ λόγος· ἱδρῶτα δὴ οὖν τὸν ἐπὶ τῷδε μέθες, αἷμα δὲ ποῖον ἂν εἴη πάλιν ὃ καὶ προσκομίζειν ἔθος, τὸν τῶν ἱερῶν ἡγούμενον ὑπέρ τε ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων, ἐρομένῳ φράσον.
pass_a_gloss: [Paul's quotation continued from §17, Hebrews 9:6–12:] into the first tent continually (διὰ παντός) the priests enter (εἴσειμι) accomplishing (ἐπιτελέω) the services/worships (λατρεῖαι); but into the second, once (ἅπαξ) of the year, alone the high priest (ἀρχιερεύς), not without blood (αἷμα), which he offers (προσφέρω) for himself and the ignorances (ἀγνοήματα) of the people; the Holy Spirit making clear (δηλόω) this: that not yet has been manifested (φανερόω) the way (ὁδός) of the holies while the first tent still has standing (στάσις). Which [is] a parable/figure (παραβολή) for the present (ἐνεστηκώς) time, according to which gifts (δῶρα) and sacrifices (θυσίαι) are offered, not able according to conscience (συνείδησις) to perfect (τελειόω) the worshiper (λατρεύων), only upon foods and drinks and various washings (βαπτισμοί), ordinances (δικαιώματα) of flesh laid upon [them] until a time of setting-right/reformation (διόρθωσις). But Christ, having arrived (παραγίνομαι) as high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tent not handmade (χειροποίητος), that is, not of this creation (κτίσις), nor through blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered once-for-all (ἐφάπαξ) into the Holies of holies, having found (εὑρίσκω) eternal redemption (λύτρωσις). You understand then that the services in the first tent the priests accomplished, not having the running-in/entry (εἰσδρομή) into the Holies of holies. For such somehow is the worship according to law, having standing in shadows (σκιαί). And these things [are] vain/useless (εἰκαῖος) for cleansing (κάθαρσις) and washing-off (ἀπόπλυσις) of sin. For you learned just now, Paul crying out, that they are incapable (ἀνικάνως ἔχω) according to conscience of perfecting the worshiper. Rather it was kept (διατηρέω) until the time of reformation, clearly [that] of the inhumanation (ἐνανθρώπησις) of the Only-begotten (Μονογενής), when the unloveliness (τὸ ἀκαλλές) of the types changed over (μεταχωρέω) into truth (ἀλήθεια). 'Once of the year and alone the high priest used to enter into the Holies of holies, and not without blood, which he brought (προσάγω) for himself and the ignorances of the people.' Most wise Paul will make clear (σαφηνίζω) this also again, saying thus about Christ: 'Saying above: sacrifices and offerings (προσφοραί) and whole burnt offerings (ὁλοκαυτώματα) and [offerings] for sin you did not will (θέλω) nor were pleased (εὐδοκέω), which are offered according to law; then I said: Behold I have come to do your will (θέλημα).' He takes away (ἀναιρέω) the first that he may set up (ἵστημι) the second; 'in which will we have been sanctified (ἁγιάζω) through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ; and every high priest stands daily ministering (λειτουργέω) and offering often the same sacrifices, which can never strip off (περιαιρέω) sins; [printed οὐδεμίαν 'no', read οὗτος δὲ μίαν 'but this one'] having offered one sacrifice for sins, sat (καθίζω) in perpetuity (εἰς τὸ διηνεκές) at the right of God, henceforth awaiting (ἐκδέχομαι) until his enemies are put a footstool (ὑποπόδιον) of his feet; for by one offering he has perfected in perpetuity those being sanctified.' For having died once he no longer dies, according to the written [word]; and having carried up (ἀναφέρω) sins of many, he entered into the Holies of holies, that is, into heaven, now to be manifested (ἐμφανίζω) to the face (πρόσωπον) of God for us. PALL.: Clear [is] the account; so then let go (μεθίημι) the sweat (ἱδρώς) upon this; and what blood would it be again which [it was] custom (ἔθος) also to bring (προσκομίζω), [for] the leader of the priests (ὁ τῶν ἱερῶν ἡγούμενος), for himself and the ignorances of the people, tell (φράζω) [me] asking.
pass_b_english: Cyril: ‘…the priests continually go into the first tent, performing the services; but into the second the high priest goes alone, once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people. By this the Holy Spirit makes clear that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing. This is a figure for the present time, in which gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper as to the conscience; they deal only with foods and drinks and various washings, ordinances of the flesh imposed until a time of reformation. But Christ, having come as high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tent not made with hands, that is, not of this creation, and not through the blood of goats and calves but through his own blood, entered once for all into the Holy of Holies, having obtained eternal redemption’ (Hebrews 9:6–12).

You understand, then, that the priests performed the services in the first tent but had no way of entry into the Holy of Holies. For such, in a way, is the worship under the law: it has its standing in shadows. And these things are of no use for cleansing and washing away sin. For you heard Paul just now cry out that they cannot perfect the worshiper as to the conscience (Hebrews 9:9). Rather, it was kept until the time of reformation (Hebrews 9:10), which plainly means the time when the Only-begotten became man, when what was unlovely in the types passed over into the truth. ‘Once a year the high priest alone used to enter the Holy of Holies, and not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people’ (Hebrews 9:7). The most wise Paul will make this plain to us again, speaking of Christ in these words: ‘When he said above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin you did not desire, nor did you take pleasure in them” (these are offered according to the law), “then I said, Behold, I have come to do your will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second. By that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ. And every high priest stands day after day ministering and offering again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins; but he, having offered one sacrifice for sins, sat down for ever at the right hand of God, waiting from then on until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet. For by one offering he has perfected for ever those who are being sanctified’ (Hebrews 10:8–14). For having died once, he dies no more, as it is written (Romans 6:9–10); and having borne the sins of many (Hebrews 9:28), he entered into the Holy of Holies, that is, into heaven, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf (Hebrews 9:24).

Palladius: Your explanation is clear. So you may leave off your labor on that point. But tell me, since I ask: what blood, again, was the one who presides over the sacred rites accustomed to bring for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people?

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-quotation: Paul's Hebrews 9:6–12 begun at the end of §17 continues across the column break (PG 68.684); labelled 'Cyril:' because the quotation is in his turn. Cyril's text of Hebrews 9:12 reads εἰς Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων ('into the Holy of Holies') where the New Testament has εἰς τὰ ἅγια; and Hebrews 9:9 has καθ' ὃν (referring to the time) where most New Testament texts read καθ' ἥν. Both translated as Cyril has them. The second 'Once a year...' (Hebrews 9:7) is Cyril's restatement in the past tense; it is in quotation marks in the print and cited. Hebrews 10:8–9 quotes Psalm 40:6–8 (LXX Psalm 39:7–9) and 10:13 echoes Psalm 110:1 (LXX 109:1); the citation is given to Hebrews, the passage Cyril quotes. Hebrews 10:11: Cyril's text reads ἀρχιερεύς ('every high priest'), a reading also found in part of the New Testament manuscript tradition; most printed texts have ἱερεύς ('every priest'). Translated 'high priest' as printed. Hebrews 10:12: the printed Greek (PG 68.684) reads οὐδεμίαν ('no sacrifice'), which reverses the verse; the English follows οὗτος δὲ μίαν ('but He, having offered one sacrifice'), the New Testament reading. An earlier lane reported that the Latin version printed beside it in PG 68.683 reads 'hic autem, cum unam pro peccatis hostiam obtulisset'; I did not re-check the Latin column myself. 'For ever' in 10:12 is placed with 'sat down'; the Greek εἰς τὸ διηνεκές can also go with 'offered one sacrifice for sins'. 'Having died once, He dies no more, as it is written' joins Romans 6:9 (οὐκέτι ἀποθνήσκει) and 6:10 (ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ). 'The types, which had no beauty of their own, gave way to the truth' renders τῶν τύπων τὸ ἀκαλλὲς μετακεχώρηκεν εἰς ἀλήθειαν (literally 'the unloveliness of the types changed over into truth'). Palladius' ἱδρῶτα ... μέθες ('let go the sweat on this') is taken as 'you may put down your labor on that point'. Reviewer: Hebrews 10:9 in Cyril's printed text reads τότε εἶπον ('then I said', the wording of Psalm 40:7, LXX 39:8) where the New Testament has τότε εἴρηκεν ('then he said'); translated as printed. The words 'He takes away the first in order to establish the second' (Hebrews 10:9b) stand outside the quotation marks in the print; they are verbatim Hebrews and kept inside the cited quotation. Palladius' τὸν τῶν ἱερῶν ἡγούμενον: ἱερῶν is the neuter 'sacred rites' (priests would be ἱερέων), so 'the one who presides over the sacred rites', not 'the chief of the priests'. πάλιν in Σαφηνιεῖ ... πάλιν restored as 'again'. The Hebrews 10:12 emendation (οὐδεμίαν → οὗτος δὲ μίαν) is accepted: the printed word contradicts the verse and Cyril's own next sentence; the Latin column was not re-checked in this review.

Hebrews 10:9 τότε εἶπον translated as printed 'then I said' (was 'then he said', the NT wording); noted
